title: Why Didn't You Use The Dry Run Option?

title: chat-mach-dude, put this show on this device now, kthxbai
raw_fallback: Callback to an October 5, 2017 Facebook post about a Slim Jim/PlutoTV commercial parody, 8 years and 11 months later.

localized_content.professional: Reflecting on an October 2017 social media post satirizing early streaming-service advertising, in the context of the intervening evolution of natural-language voice interfaces for media control. What required a multi-step manual remote workflow in 2017 is now expressed as a single conversational utterance to an assistant.
localized_content.spencer: found an old post from October 2017, some dumb bit about a Slim Jim commercial on plutoTV with an amish buggy in it. read it again tonight and just went 'damn, now I just do something like "chat-mach-dude, put this show on this device now,kthxbai" and it just does it.' no amish buggy required. 8 years and 11 months and the whole bit is just... obsolete. wild timeline, dot dot dot.
localized_content.ninja: Legacy 2017 signal intercepted and re-analyzed. Manual remote-control vectors fully deprecated. Single-utterance command injection now handles target device state directly. Silent, immediate, no physical interface required.
localized_content.pirate: Dug up an old log from October 2017 -- a tale of amish buggies and slim jims on the crow's nest television. Now, arr, I just bark the order at me first mate 'chat-mach-dude' and the show sails onto the screen without so much as raisin' a sail. Nigh eight years since that log, and the old ways be dead and buried.
localized_content.HwOps: Pulled an old ticket from October 2017 -- some bit about a Slim Jim ad on plutoTV. Back then, putting a show on meant hands on a physical remote, menus, the whole dance. Now it's one line: 'chat-mach-dude, put this show on this device now, kthxbai.' We don't simulate the interface anymore; we just say the command and it runs.
